newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-Doctors say breaks needed in test rugby.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-Doctors say breaks needed in test rugby.

text.p: DUNEDIN, Aug 18 - Medical teams for the All Blacks and Wallabies have united to try and persuade their respective rugby unions to either space out test matches or implement meaningful breaks to allow time for rest and rehabilitation, NZPA reports.
The demand on players in the Super 12 and the Tri-Series has been unfair and if the current pressure continued, matches would lose quality gradually, they said.

"I feel that, after having lived with these guys for 2-1/2 to three months and seen what what they've been through, I think we need to put a structure in place to make sure that players have had adequate rest and rehabilitation from a very hard
series like this," All Black doctor John Mayhew said.

Australian team doctor John Best believes there should be a couple of weeks break between the Super 12 and the Tri-Series and another three-week layoff for players after the Tri-Series. He has made the recommendation to the Australian Rugby Union.

Dr Mayhew treated at least 10 players for injuries after the All Blacks' 36-24 win over the Wallabies at Carisbrook on Saturday, saying they would need a couple of weeks' break before playing in the national provincial championships.
All Black coach John Hart has pleaded with provincial coaches to use their commonsense and allow their regular test players some rest.
He is concerned with burnout, the players having started training in February for the Super 12 and continued on virtually every week until the weekend when the Tri-Series came to an end.
However, the national championships have already got underway and some coaches are demanding their All Blacks to make themselves available immediately.
Hart said North Harbour suffered last season when their players returned from the Tri-Series and started playing provincial games immediately.
"Player welfare needs a serious look," he said.
"We'll downgrade the product ultimately and we will certainly shorten the careers of the top players if we carry on the way we are."
He said only regular test players needed a break before playing in the provincial games.
"I'm very supportive of the NPC (provincial games), we need it to keep players in shape before the tour Britain.
"If they don't get the break, then we're going to pick up some tired pieces at the end of the year that is not going to benefit the All Blacks or the NPC."
Players like Zinzan Brooke and Josh Kronfeld have been showing signs of fatigue in the last couple of weeks.
"I think it's something that I can caress the rugby union to look at to mandate," Dr Mayhew said of the spaces needed between major competitions.
"We're just expecting too much from our players to play test rugby for eight games and then suddenly go back and play for North Harbour or Auckland or whatever," he said.
Brooke said it was getting harder and harder to recover between tests as the games were drawn so closely.
